patches.old: From an SDT perspective, adaptation shifts the signal-plus-noise distribution downward—the adapted stimulus produces less internal activation, making it harder to detect and effectively raising the criterion relative to the stimulus.
patches.new: From an SDT perspective, adaptation moves the signal-plus-noise distribution toward the noise distribution: the adapted stimulus now produces less internal activation, the two distributions overlap more, and d′ falls. Note that this is a change in **sensitivity**, not in bias — the observer's criterion need not move at all. The same logic applies to added background noise, which widens and raises the noise distribution and so lowers d′.

patches.old: The **criterion** (also called **beta, β**, or the decision threshold) is the internal activation level above which the observer will say "yes, signal present."
patches.new: The **criterion** (the decision threshold) is the internal activation level above which the observer will say "yes, signal present." Its position is reported either as **c**, the location of the line itself, or as **β**, the likelihood ratio at that line; the two are different numbers for the same idea, and the MCAT treats either as the measure of response bias, in contrast to d′.

patches.old: - **Brightness (vision)**: k ≈ 0.02 (2%) — you need only a 2% change in light intensity to notice a difference
patches.new: - **Brightness (vision)**: k ≈ 0.08 (8%) — you need roughly an 8% change in light intensity to notice a difference

- **Smell**: k ≈ 0.07–0.10 (7–10%), varying widely with the odorant

These constants are approximations. Published Weber fractions for the same modality differ substantially across studies and stimulus conditions, so treat the ordering — weight and vision fine, taste and smell coarse — as the point, and expect the exam to test the proportionality rather than the exact constants.

visual.title: The two distributions, the four outcomes and Weber's fraction
visual.alt: Overlapping normal distributions for noise alone and signal plus noise, with d-prime marked as the distance between their peaks and a vertical criterion line that can slide left for a liberal bias or right for a conservative one; a two-by-two table of hit, miss, false alarm and correct rejection with their clinical equivalents; and a bar chart of Weber fractions from heaviness and brightness at two per cent up to loudness at ten per cent.
visual.caption: Hits and false alarms moving together means the line moved. Only a change in the gap between the two curves is a change in sensitivity.
